To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the SER of one-bit precoded massive MIMO can be interpreted as the SER with infinite-resolution precoding and a constellation range that is $\sqrt{2 / \pi }$ smaller, and 2) the one-bit precoding performance is within 2  dB of that of infinite-resolution precoding.

the QAM constellation range for one-bit precoder can be chosen the same as that of the infinite resolution case, except for a scaling factor of $\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi }}$ and that the one-bit precoding performance can be within 2 dB of infinite resolution case, if the number of antennas is increased by 50%.

the QAM constellation range for one-bit precoders is about 80% of that for infinite-resolution precoders with per-symbol power constraints and that one-bit precoders require about 50% extra antennas for achieving the same performance as the infinite-resolution ZF precoders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question of massive MIMO with one-bit precoded QAM signaling, which is of practical relevance for massive MIMO implementation with low-resolution DACs.
the design of one-bit symbol-level massive MIMO precoding for QAM modulation.
the design of low-resolution DACs for massive MIMO.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
one-bit precoding provides a 0.8-1 dB performance degradation compared to infinite-resolution precoding in massive MIMO.
one-bit precoding with the proposed design is a promising candidate for the massive MIMO downlink transmission.
one-bit precoding with QAM signaling requires about 2 dB and 50% more number of antennas than infinite-resolution precoding to achieve the same error performance in massive MIMO downlink.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of one-bit DACs in massive MIMO is not a good idea, but the gap between one-bit DAC and infinite-resolution DACs is not too large either.
the use of one-bit DACs in massive MIMO is a practical and promising option for future energy-efficient 5G systems.
one-bit precoding with QAM signaling requires about 50\% more antennas to reach the same performance as the infinite-resolution precoder with per-symbol power control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for massive MIMO, a reasonable choice of constellation range for one-bit precoders is the infinite-resolution ZF with per-symbol power constraints.
one-bit precoding provides a significant energy efficiency advantage over the infinite-resolution precoders at the cost of a 2 dB performance loss.
the use of one-bit precoders is a promising approach for achieving the energy efficiency advantage of massive MIMO systems.
